Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you turn this into a usable prompt for a proposed weekly schedule at harborlight community radio, for the week of october 5 to 11, 2026. we are a small independent station in north cove, not a commercial music service, and the schedule should feel like something our volunteers could actually run. ask for a schedule covering 6 a.m. to midnight each day. include program names, start and end times, whether something is live or recorded, and the host when we have one. this is a proposal, not an announcement that anything has been approved.

some background to carry through: harborlight broadcasts from a converted net loft above the ferry office, serves north cove and three nearby islands, and has a small online stream for former residents. we have six paid staff and around twenty regular volunteers. the station’s purpose is local news, music and practical information; it is not meant to sound like a tourism advert. listeners include ferry workers, fishers, students at the technical college, and people who are at home during the day. please make the schedule readable to that mix of people, but don't write promotional copy or invent listener research.

there are fixed programs that must stay in place. “Morning Window” airs weekdays from 6 to 9 a.m., hosted live by Mara Venn, with weather, ferry notices and local headlines. “North Cove at Noon” is live weekdays from noon to 1 p.m.; its rotating hosts are Ivo Bell and Tess Rowan, and the schedule can say rotating host rather than choosing one. “Harbor News” is live weekdays from 5 to 6 p.m., produced by the newsroom and hosted by Saira Cole. “Night Signals,” a recorded music program hosted by Ren Okafor, is already committed on Tuesday and Thursday from 9 to 11 p.m. Do not move these shows, rename them, or change their live/recorded status.

we need some room for shows that are ready or nearly ready. “Tide Table” is a 30-minute recorded practical segment with fisheries adviser Lou Chen, and can run twice in the week, but not before 8 a.m. “Workshop Radio” is a live 60-minute student-made music and interview show; the technical college studio is only available Wednesday after 7 p.m. and the student host Nessa Pike cannot stay past 9 p.m. “Borrowed Books” is a recorded 30-minute library conversation, delivered by librarian Ollie Hart, and may be placed on any day after 10 a.m. The monthly “Island Desk” interview is not ready this week, so leave it out rather than listing a placeholder. A volunteer has proposed a new local music hour called “Low Water”; we have no confirmed host or recording yet, so don’t present it as a ready program.

there are routine services to account for too. A two-minute weather and ferry update is prepared each morning by 5:45, including weekends, and can be listed at 5:55 a.m. daily. The emergency office wants its test message at 11:58 a.m. on Wednesday, but it is only a test and should be labelled that way, not described as an actual warning. Saturday’s farmers and fishers market opens at 8 a.m.; the outside broadcast team can do a live 45-minute report between 8 and 10, but the van must be back at the station by 10:30. The team lead, Jo Mercer, says, “We can carry a microphone and one recorder, not the whole studio.” There is no Sunday outside broadcast crew.

we also have an offer from the county radio relay desk for a live one-hour coastal weather feed. we do not know yet whether the line will be available, and the desk will confirm by Thursday at 3 p.m. If the desk confirms the feed by then, schedule it Saturday from 7 to 8 p.m. and move the recorded repeat of “Dockside Notes” from Sunday at 8 p.m. to Sunday at 9 p.m.; make sure the Sunday listing reflects that move. If the desk does not confirm by Thursday at 3 p.m., do not schedule the relay at all, put the recorded local “Harbor Voices” episode in the Saturday 7-to-8 p.m. slot instead, and leave “Dockside Notes” at Sunday 8 p.m. Do not show both alternatives as if both are happening. “Dockside Notes” is a recorded 30-minute conversation with boat repairers, and “Harbor Voices” is a recorded one-hour collection of oral histories. Neither has a live host.

please observe these practical limits as you build the week:
1. No single live host should be assigned to overlapping programs, and do not put Nessa’s show outside its Wednesday studio window or after 9 p.m.
2. Do not invent a host for a show whose host is not specified. For an unhosted recorded item, mark it recorded and leave the host field blank or say “no live host.”
3. Keep the fixed weekday programs at their stated times, keep “Night Signals” on Tuesday and Thursday, and do not list “Island Desk” or “Low Water” as scheduled this week.
4. Use the confirmed-by-Thursday relay condition and its alternative exactly as stated above. The decision changes the Sunday “Dockside Notes” time as well as the Saturday 7-to-8 p.m. listing.

make the result a clear day-by-day schedule, with times in a consistent format and enough detail to distinguish each program without writing episode scripts. Include short notes for the Wednesday test message and Saturday market report so a volunteer can tell what they are. If a slot has no supplied program, label it as open or unscheduled rather than making up a show. A brief note at the top can explain that this is a proposed schedule and that the relay listing depends on Thursday’s confirmation, but don’t imply that confirmation has happened.

at the end, include a short operational note explaining that the Saturday market team has to return the van by 10:30 a.m., that there is no Sunday outside broadcast crew, and that the relay decision must be reflected in the Sunday listing as well as Saturday’s. Keep that final note substantive and consistent with whichever conditional wording the prompt asks the schedule-maker to use. We need a complete prompt that preserves all of this information and asks for the schedule; please don’t draft the schedule itself.", "output": "Create a proposed weekly schedule for Harborlight Community Radio for October 5–11, 2026. This is a proposal, not an announcement of an approved schedule. Cover 6 a.m. to midnight each day. For every scheduled program, show its name, start and end times, whether it is live or recorded, and its host when specified. Use a clear day-by-day format and consistent time notation. Include enough information to distinguish each program, but do not write episode scripts. Label any slot without a supplied program as open or unscheduled rather than inventing a show.

## Station context
Harborlight is a small independent station in North Cove, broadcasting from a converted net loft above the ferry office. It serves North Cove and three nearby islands, with a small online stream for former residents. The station has six paid staff and about twenty regular volunteers. Its purpose is local news, music, and practical information, not tourism promotion. Its listeners include ferry workers, fishers, technical-college students, and people at home during the day. Make the schedule readable to this audience. Do not write promotional copy or invent listener research.

## Programs that must remain as scheduled
- **Morning Window:** Weekdays, 6–9 a.m.; live, hosted by Mara Venn. Includes weather, ferry notices, and local headlines.
- **North Cove at Noon:** Weekdays, noon–1 p.m.; live, with rotating hosts Ivo Bell and Tess Rowan. List the host as “rotating host”; do not choose between them.
- **Harbor News:** Weekdays, 5–6 p.m.; live, produced by the newsroom and hosted by Saira Cole.
- **Night Signals:** Tuesday and Thursday, 9–11 p.m.; recorded music program hosted by Ren Okafor.

Do not move or rename these programs, or change their live/recorded status.

## Programs available for this week
- **Tide Table:** A 30-minute recorded practical segment with fisheries adviser Lou Chen. It may air twice during the week, but not before 8 a.m.
- **Workshop Radio:** A live, 60-minute student-made music and interview show. The technical-college studio is available only Wednesday after 7 p.m. Student host Nessa Pike cannot stay past 9 p.m. Schedule the show only within those limits.
- **Borrowed Books:** A recorded, 30-minute library conversation delivered by librarian Ollie Hart. It may air any day after 10 a.m.
- **Island Desk:** This monthly interview is not ready this week. Leave it out; do not use a placeholder.
- **Low Water:** A proposed local music hour without a confirmed host or recording. Do not present it as ready or schedule it.

## Regular services and outside broadcasts
A two-minute weather and ferry update is prepared by 5:45 a.m. every day, including weekends. It may be listed at 5:55 a.m. daily. At 11:58 a.m. Wednesday, include the emergency office’s test message and label it clearly as a test, not as an actual warning.

On Saturday, the farmers and fishers market opens at 8 a.m. The outside broadcast team can provide a live 45-minute report between 8 and 10 a.m., but the van must be back at the station by 10:30 a.m. Team lead Jo Mercer says, “We can carry a microphone and one recorder, not the whole studio.” There is no Sunday outside broadcast crew. Include a short note that makes the Saturday report and its limits clear.

## Conditional relay and alternative
The county radio relay desk has offered a live, one-hour coastal weather feed, but its line availability is not yet known. The desk will confirm by Thursday at 3 p.m. Apply exactly one of these alternatives:

- **If the desk confirms the feed by Thursday at 3 p.m.:** Schedule the relay Saturday from 7 to 8 p.m. Move the recorded repeat of “Dockside Notes” from Sunday at 8 p.m. to Sunday at 9 p.m., and ensure that the Sunday listing shows the new time.
- **If the desk does not confirm by Thursday at 3 p.m.:** Do not schedule the relay. Put the recorded local “Harbor Voices” episode in the Saturday 7-to-8 p.m. slot instead, and leave “Dockside Notes” at Sunday 8 p.m.

Do not list both alternatives as though both will happen. “Dockside Notes” is a recorded, 30-minute conversation with boat repairers. “Harbor Voices” is a recorded, one-hour collection of oral histories. Neither has a live host. The relay decision affects both Saturday’s 7-to-8 p.m. listing and the Sunday “Dockside Notes” time.

## Scheduling limits
1. Do not assign one live host to overlapping programs. Keep Nessa Pike’s show within the Wednesday studio window and end it no later than 9 p.m.
2. Do not invent a host when none is specified. For an unhosted recorded item, mark it as recorded and leave the host field blank or write “no live host.”
3. Keep the fixed weekday programs at their stated times, keep “Night Signals” on Tuesday and Thursday, and do not schedule “Island Desk” or “Low Water” this week.
4. Apply the relay condition and its alternative as stated above, including the resulting change—or lack of change—to Sunday’s “Dockside Notes” listing.

At the top, you may include a brief note saying that the schedule is proposed and that the relay listing depends on Thursday’s confirmation. Do not imply that confirmation has already happened. End with a substantive operational note stating that the Saturday market team must return the van by 10:30 a.m., there is no Sunday outside broadcast crew, and the relay decision must be reflected in both Saturday’s listing and Sunday’s listing. Keep the note consistent with the conditional schedule."}]
